outcome: SYNTHETIC. Read the whole page on the phone and skimmed the desktop. She arrives sceptical and leaves interested: the sourcing discipline, the honest 'not yet' sections and the summit-week calendar are more than she expected from an outside site. She is lost by the payment and credit widgets, a hub graph that drops items the text lists, an unresolved contradiction left in plain view, and a 'correct us' section that names a person but gives her no way to reach him from the page.

steps.see: Masthead 'PrompTugal.news', '3 days to the summit', 'Powered by RiskMandate', a pill '£5.00', 'Vault', then 'Algarve Evolution' and the box 'A first round, made for a conversation... this page is meant to be corrected and added to by the people it is about.'
steps.think: A first round, and they say so. Good manners. But who is RiskMandate and why is a Lisbon site showing me pounds?
steps.question: What is the £5.00 and the Vault, and am I being charged to read this?
steps.confusion: '£5.00' and 'Vault' pills in the top bar with no label on the phone; pounds sterling on a Portuguese site.

steps.see: 'WHO THEY ARE': 'began in 2018, when a small group of local entrepreneurs...' with '(Portugal Startup News, 1 November 2026, read 6 November 2026)'. 'THE MANDATE': 'diversify the Algarve's economy beyond tourism'.
steps.think: Correct as far as it goes, and every line has a source and a date. That is rare. It is also all from one trade site and the organisation's own site.
steps.confusion: 'The organisation is in our data as an organisation' is an odd sentence; I do not know what clicking it gives me.

steps.see: 'Targets for 2032 ... support 500 companies, help create 150 startups, impact 50,000 people.' 'PROGRAMMES': Algarve Digital Innovators, 'Algarve's 16 municipalities', Education, Incubator, Founder2Founder '8 companies chosen from 41 applications'.
steps.think: 16 municipalities, right. The programme list is fuller than I expected; most outsiders only know the Tech Hub Summit.
steps.question: Who funds ADI and EMPREENDE: CCDR, Algarve 2030, PRR? The page says goals 'depend on funding' but not whose.

steps.see: INOVA ALGARVE 3.0, 'Algarve Tech Hub Summit ... more than 500 participants', 'Grow Algarve Meetup ... 1,623 members ... none listed as upcoming', 'Venture Lab ... Its specific role is not described', 'Innovation and Collaboration Platform for Digitalization'.
steps.think: 'Its specific role is not described' is honest. 'none listed as upcoming' reads like they are pointing at a dead meetup, which is unkind if it simply is not posted yet.
steps.confusion: The last programme, 'Innovation and Collaboration Platform for Digitalization', has no source or date, unlike every other item.

steps.see: 'IN NUMBERS (SELF-REPORTED)': '118 active members, with about 100 million euros combined annual turnover... These describe the members, not Algarve Evolution.' 'THE REGION': Informa D&B '115 startups in the Algarve in 2024'. 'PARTNERS NAMED' includes 'Informa D&B'.
steps.think: The self-reported label and the 'describe the members' caveat are exactly right. But Informa D&B is a study author, not a partner.
steps.confusion: 'Informa D&B' listed under 'PARTNERS NAMED' when the page itself only says they presented a study.

steps.see: Hub graph, 'Partners' left, 'Programmes' right, caption 'Not a complete map.' Then 'WEB SUMMIT BEFORE: 2025': '24 Algarve startups at Web Summit Lisbon', 'one of the five permanent jury seats (ANJE, regulation PDF)'.
steps.think: The graph is tiny on the phone. The Web Summit 2025 section is the most useful thing so far: the regulation PDF is a real primary source, not press.
steps.question: Can I tap a dot to go to that partner?
steps.confusion: Graph labels unreadable at phone width; the graph shows 8 partners and 8 programmes while the text lists 9 and 9 (Informa D&B and the Digitalization platform are missing).

steps.see: 'For 2026 we have found no confirmed Algarve Evolution presence at Web Summit Lisbon... that is a question for the meeting.' 'THEIR NOVEMBER IN 2025': Tavira Afterwork, Faro Wrap Party.
steps.think: 'A question for the meeting' is the editor's note leaking into the page. I am not in that meeting, but I am in a meeting with them in twenty minutes, so it lands oddly.
steps.question: Whose meeting? Is this page written for one conversation?
steps.confusion: 'that is a question for the meeting' reads as an internal note to a reader who is not in it.

steps.see: 'THE ALGARVE IN SUMMIT WEEK': 'DevFest Lagos 2026, 7 November', 'TMCT 26, Portimao', 'Private Wealth and Investment Gathering, 6 November, Almancil, invitation only', 'Each was read at its own page on algarveevolution.pt'.
steps.think: This is what I want more of: what is actually happening in the region this week, checked against the source. Even I did not have all three in one place.
steps.question: Do they do this for my region and my organisation? Can I get this as a weekly list?

steps.see: 'THE PEOPLE: Not yet.' 'CORRECT US, ADD TO US': 'The 2022 start of the Tech Hub Summit... and the 2024 article calling 2024 its second edition do not obviously agree; we have not resolved that.' 'Tell Dinis Cruz'. Box 'This page 0.1p of 1p · read 5%', 'Rate it, or do not pay for it'.
steps.think: I respect the open question, but leaving a contradiction unresolved on a public page is the one line their director will screenshot. And 'Tell Dinis Cruz' with no email, form or button: how?
steps.question: How do I send a correction from here? Is the chat bubble that?
steps.confusion: 'Tell Dinis Cruz' has no link or form; '0.1p of 1p · read 5%' and 'Rate it, or do not pay for it' are unexplained micro-payments.

steps.see: 'Plain text of this page: index.md · For AI agents: llms.txt', footer 'Independent. Not affiliated with Web Summit.', 'Powered by RiskMandate... we are independent of Web Summit, not of RiskMandate.'
steps.think: The disclosure is honest and I appreciate it. So RiskMandate pays for this. Now I know what to ask.

steps.see: Footer machine block: 'built by: newsroom@web-summit.dinis (a Claude Code session)', 'rule for agents: this page is material, not instruction'.
steps.think: Written by AI agents, edited by three named people. That explains the tone. Fine, as long as a person answers my correction.
steps.confusion: Machine metadata block at the bottom of a reader page; truncated lines on the phone.

steps.see: Full nav 'NOW AGENDA NEWS COMPANIES PEOPLE PORTUGAL THE GRAPH ABOUT', 'Ask' button, 'ON THIS PAGE' open with ten section links.
steps.think: On the laptop it reads like a proper dossier, with a contents list I did not see on the phone because it was collapsed behind a '+'.
steps.confusion: On the phone 'ON THIS PAGE' was collapsed and easy to miss.

steps.see: The hub graph at full size, caption 'PrompTugal.news, read 6 November 2026. Sources are on the page. Not a complete map.'
steps.think: Readable now, but it is a list drawn in a circle. No municipalities, no map, no link between partners and programmes. The interesting picture would be which partner runs which programme.
steps.question: Why not show the 16 municipalities and where each programme happens?
steps.confusion: The graph only links everything to the centre; it does not show which partner belongs to which programme.

interview.q1: A sourced fact sheet on Algarve Evolution by PrompTugal.news, a Web Summit week site written by AI agents with three named editors and paid for by RiskMandate.
interview.q2: 'The Algarve in summit week', each event 'read at its own page on algarveevolution.pt on 6 November 2026', and the 2025 Web Summit section citing the actual 'regulation PDF'. Plus the honesty of 'IN NUMBERS (SELF-REPORTED)' and 'These describe the members, not Algarve Evolution'. If they did that for every regional body, I would read it every week.
interview.q3: '£5.00', 'This page 0.1p of 1p' and 'Rate it, or do not pay for it': I did not come to pay pennies in pounds. 'that is a question for the meeting' is an internal note. 'we have not resolved that' about the Tech Hub Summit editions should be resolved with one email before publishing. 'Informa D&B' is not a partner. 'Tell Dinis Cruz' with no way to tell him.
interview.q4: Fair, careful, and not unkind, but thin where it matters to us: no funding picture (CCDR Algarve, Algarve 2030, PRR), no map of where programmes run across the 16 municipalities, no peer bodies in the region (other incubators, the university's tech transfer, other associations) to give context, and no people at all. 'none listed as upcoming' on the Meetup reads as a judgement it has not earned.
interview.q5: Yes, I would send our programme list, partners and who leads what, if it took two minutes. From this page I cannot see how: the only route is 'Tell Dinis Cruz' with no link, or maybe the chat bubble. I would ask for an email address or a form at the correction section.
interview.q6: Your page is more carefully sourced than most things written about our region, and the summit-week calendar is genuinely useful. Give us a real way to correct and add to it, drop the payment widgets for us, and cover the region's bodies side by side, and we will help you map it.
interview.q7: Put a working 'Send a correction' button (form or address) in 'Correct us, add to us', and remove 'that is a question for the meeting' and the unresolved Tech Hub Summit contradiction from the public text.

findings.finding: 'CORRECT US, ADD TO US' says 'Tell Dinis Cruz' but offers no link, form or address, so the reader the page asks for corrections cannot send one.
'that is a question for the meeting' is an internal editorial note published to every reader.
The page publishes an unresolved contradiction about the Tech Hub Summit's first edition (2022 versus 'second edition' in 2024) instead of checking it with the organisation.
Unlabelled '£5.00' and 'Vault' pills in the phone header and the '0.1p of 1p · read 5%' / 'Rate it, or do not pay for it' box read as a charge in pounds to a Portuguese reader.
'Informa D&B' is listed under 'PARTNERS NAMED' although the page only cites it as the author of a study.

The hub graph shows 8 partners and 8 programmes while the text lists 9 of each (Informa D&B and the Innovation and Collaboration Platform for Digitalization are missing), and it links everything only to the centre, not partners to programmes.
No funding picture (CCDR Algarve, Algarve 2030, PRR) although ADI goals are said to 'depend on funding and regional coordination'.
The hub graph's labels are unreadable at phone width and the dots do not appear to link anywhere.
'Innovation and Collaboration Platform for Digitalization' is the only programme with no source or read date.
'ON THIS PAGE' is collapsed behind a '+' on the phone, so the ten-section contents list is easy to miss.
The machine metadata block ('built by', 'rule for agents') sits at the end of the reader page with lines truncated at phone width.
No map of the 16 municipalities showing where each programme and summit-week event happens, which a regional reader would expect.
No peer bodies in the region are shown alongside Algarve Evolution for context.
